info.name: Aluria ERP API v2
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for the Aluria/Venken ERP v2 API (erpAPI-v.1.0/v2) — generated from docs/api/*.md. Every request includes at least one saved example response taken directly from the source documentation (200/201 success plus the documented 400/401/403/404/405/409/410/429/500 failure cases where applicable). 

## Getting started
1. Select (or duplicate) the **Aluria ERP v2 - Local** environment and set `base_url` to your running instance (default assumes `php -S localhost:8000 router.php` from the project root, which the repo's router.php supports directly — adjust to your actual host, e.g. an nginx vhost proxying `/api/v2/...` or `/venken-api/v2/...`).
2. Set `email` / `password` in the environment to a real account, then run **Auth → Login**. Its Tests script automatically saves the returned JWT into `access_token`, `company_id`, and `user_id`.
3. Every other request in this collection inherits Bearer auth from the collection level (`Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`) — no per-request auth setup needed. The 6 public account/permission endpoints (login, send-otp, register, forgot-password, reset-password) are explicitly marked "No Auth".
4. Path parameters (`:customer_id`, `:id`, etc.) are pre-filled with realistic example values taken from the docs — edit them per-request (Postman's "Path Variables" tab under each request's URL) once you have real IDs from your own data.

## Response shape
Every endpoint returns `{ status_code, status_message, data }` (see CODE_STANDARDS.md). Auth/account endpoints additionally return an `error_code` on failures, for frontend localisation.

Source: v2/docs/api/*.md (52 module docs) plus v2/auth/{forgot-password,reset-password}.php and v2/finance/general-journal/index.php read directly (undocumented in docs/api at generation time).

request.description: Exchanges a Movira SSO code for an Aluria JWT. The frontend receives a `code` (and `state`) after the user authenticates on Movira, then calls this endpoint. The server exchanges the code with Movira's `/api/v2/sso/exchange` using X-Client-Id/X-Client-Secret credentials, verifies the user exists in app_user, and issues a JWT — same response shape as Login. Also accepts GET with `?code=...&state=...` for browser redirect callbacks. On success, the Tests script saves the token into {{access_token}}.
